quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger directs you, when there is a stop sign, or when red lights flash and gates are down.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop at any intersection.
When the traffic light is red.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at a red traffic light. Always obey a police officer's directions, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: What is a diamond-shaped sign?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are yellow warning signs. Orange diamond signs are used in work areas. These signs warn you of hazards or special rules ahead.

questions.question: You miss your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Always take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead is now divided. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and cold showers do not speed up this process.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go ahead because you have the right-of-way.
Go ahead if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, you must let any pedestrians in the intersection finish crossing before you proceed.

questions.question: The safest way to turn is to cross as few lanes as possible.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. Turn into the first available legal lane. This crossing fewer lanes is the safest method.

questions.question: What are passengers not allowed to do in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to have an open alcohol container in a moving vehicle on a public road. This applies to everyone in the car. The driver can face penalties.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who drank alcohol before driving?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they drive more carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop before reaching a school bus with flashing red lights. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a two-way road with a median, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: On which sides of your vehicle should you keep a space cushion?

options.text: Only to the left and right

questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers may keep you awake, but they do not reduce your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things struggle to stay in their lanes and control their vehicles.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: May continue or exit from your current lane
May stay in your lane and continue through
Must exit if you stay in your current lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit if you stay in your current lane
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will leave the roadway. You can change lanes to stay on the freeway, or you must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up
Keep driving but stay out of its way
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely
Stop in the middle of an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Stop until a crossing guard signals you to go
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and be ready to stop if they are in the crosswalk.

questions.question: You must slow down and yield to children playing in the street.
questions.explanation: Drive with extreme caution where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: After an accident, what should a driver do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: After an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking an over-the-counter drug?

options.text: Drive anyway, even if there are warning labels.

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving ability. If you take any medication, even cold or allergy medicine, check the label for warnings. If you are not sure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking it.

questions.question: How do alcohol and drugs affect driving skills?

options.text: They slow reaction time and coordination.

questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your nervous system. It reduces your alertness and concentration, slows your reaction time, and greatly reduces your coordination.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, how can you reduce alcohol's effects?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to remove the effects of one drink.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, you should look for a gap of ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: Before entering a freeway, find a four-second gap in traffic. This gives you and the car behind you a two-second safety distance when you merge.

questions.question: How can you spot an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, improper lane changes.
By the number of passengers in their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers on the road. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or improper lane changes, do not confront them. The safest thing to do is stay out of their way.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a vehicle?
questions.explanation: All passengers and drivers must wear seat belts in vehicles equipped with them. This includes the driver, adult passengers, and passengers under 18.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Leaving extra time to reach your destination.

questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage increases. To help prevent it, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and give yourself plenty of time to reach your destination.

questions.question: What could cause you to crash?

options.text: Taking your eyes off the road
Taking your hands off the wheel
Taking your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel is a distraction that could cause a crash.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip) always have the right-of-way. You must yield to them at all times.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights is approaching. Should you pull to the right side of the road and wait for it to pass?
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, pull immediately to the right side of the road and let it pass.

questions.question: When can you walk or stand on the roadway of an expressway?

options.text: When you are trying to wave down another car

questions.explanation: Never stop on an expressway unless there is an emergency. Never walk or stand on the roadway of an expressway.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the pedestrian and then pass them.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
questions.explanation: At intersections without traffic signals, you must give pedestrians the right-of-way. This applies to marked and unmarked crosswalks. Always yield to pedestrians, even without a crosswalk.

questions.question: You had an upsetting incident at work and are angry. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to relax before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal your intention early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.

questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: What does alcohol negatively affect?
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs judgment, perception, and emotional control. Safe driving requires all of these skills. Drinking before driving makes it impossible to drive safely.

questions.question: What is a good way to prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop for a short break every two hours on long trips to avoid fatigue. If you get drowsy, pull off the road safely and nap, or find a place to stay overnight.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next exit on a highway?
questions.explanation: Signs that give destination information are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is injured in a collision?

options.text: Move injured people far away from the road.
Move injured people to where they want to go.
Tell injured people they are fine and don't need medical help.
Do not move injured people unless you absolutely must.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move injured people unless you absolutely must.
questions.explanation: Moving a seriously injured person can cause more harm. Do not move injured people unless it is necessary to protect them from fire or other dangers. Keep them lying or sitting down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: What should you do before backing your vehicle?

options.text: Walk around the entire vehicle to make sure no person or object is behind it.
Look toward the front, sides, and rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Walk completely around your vehicle to check for people or objects behind it. Before backing, look at the front, sides, and rear. Keep looking over your right shoulder while backing. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to get the attention of other drivers.
Get out of your vehicle and wave down the next car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the interstate shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. The high speed of traffic makes it very dangerous to stand or walk on an interstate.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can strengthen the effects of both. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks would.

questions.question: When should you always use a turn signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling helps other drivers know what you are doing and prevents accidents.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light is in their favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals standing near the road?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Swerve quickly into the next lane.

questions.explanation: Slow down and drive with caution if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be near the road out of sight.

questions.question: Which medications could make it harder to drive safely?
questions.explanation: Any medication could affect your ability to drive safely. Ask your doctor or pharmacist how your prescription may affect your driving. Read the labels on over-the-counter medications to see if they can impair your driving.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you wear your seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn only behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices in crashes. For the best protection, wear both your lap and shoulder seat belts along with the airbags.

questions.question: When should drivers watch out for deer and moose?

options.text: At dusk, at dawn, and during the night.

questions.correctAnswerText: At dusk, at dawn, and during the night.
questions.explanation: Deer and moose are most active at dawn and dusk. They also travel at night. Be extra careful after sunset. Dark-colored animals are hard to see until your headlights hit them.

questions.question: What does alcohol harm while driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol makes it harder for your brain to react and focus. A driver who drinks is more likely to fall asleep or leave the road. The more someone drinks, the less control they have over their body movements.

questions.question: When should drivers use turn signals?

options.text: When entering or exiting the freeway

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes, entering or exiting the freeway, and turning. This helps other drivers see your moves and avoid accidents.

questions.question: What should you do if a police officer stops you?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and tell any passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: What do large flashing arrow panels mean?

options.text: Drivers may stay in their current lane.
There is something to look at in the direction of the arrow.
Drivers should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.
questions.explanation: Large flashing arrow panels are used in construction areas where a lane is closed. Slow down and merge in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: When a blind or partially blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use guide dogs or white canes. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in the lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if flashing red lights are on, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible and close to the crossing. If you are unsure, stop. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. When you see a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop. Do not go until it is safe and clear for you to pass through the intersection.
